changes: Infinity 1.0.7: the Infinity now rolls its own parts. The game rolls parts from a list it only builds for guns loaded from the game files, so the mod now builds that list for the Infinity.
Infinity 1.0.7: checks whether the Infinity can be written to a save, and which recipe the Grinder picked, and writes it to infinity_log.txt (the Grinder still reports it couldn't make the item).
Infinity 1.0.6: the Grinder now makes the Infinity. Its item pool had a chance worked out from the Grinder that came to zero, so grinding failed and nothing came out.

Infinity 1.0.6: the Infinity now gets its own barrel (no ammo use, figure-8 shots), skin, title and Dva accessory. The parts were weighted the Borderlands 2 way, which the Pre-Sequel reads as zero, so it came out with a normal Vladof pistol's parts.

Infinity 1.0.5: writes what the Grinder does to infinity_log.txt (the recipe check, the grind and what came out), and checks once per game that the game can make an Infinity. New console command infinity_give puts one in your backpack for testing.
When the version lock sends you back to the menu, the launcher now downloads the new version straight away instead of waiting up to an hour, and installs it as soon as you close the game.
The launcher checks GitHub for updates every couple of minutes instead of once an hour.
Krieg 2.5.2: the "You must update your launcher and mods" message now shows as a box on the Pre-Sequel's menu (it wasn't showing before).

Infinity 1.0.4: the mod now finishes setting up the Infinity and its Grinder recipe. 1.0.3 started but stopped on a Borderlands 2 setting the Pre-Sequel doesn't have, so the Grinder still gave a normal gun.

Infinity 1.0.3: the Grinder gave a normal pistol instead of an Infinity because the mod never started its setup. It now starts reliably and puts its recipe back whenever Concordia reloads the Grinder.
Infinity 1.0.3: an Infinity now saves and loads like any other gun (it's listed under the names the Pre-Sequel already keeps for it).
Infinity 1.0.2: the Grinder recipe now takes any purple pistol instead of only a purple Vladof pistol. A legendary pistol, any legendary weapon and any purple pistol make an Infinity.

Infinity 1.0.1: new Grinder recipe. A legendary pistol, any legendary weapon and a purple Vladof pistol make an Infinity. This recipe comes before the game's own "two legendaries and a purple pistol" recipe, so these three always give an Infinity.

New mod for the Pre-Sequel: Infinity. Borderlands 2's Infinity pistol is now its own mod, so you can install or remove it separately from Krieg, and it works with every character. Install it from the Pre-Sequel's mods in the launcher. Three purple Vladof pistols in the Grinder make an Infinity, and every one rolls its own element, accessory, grip and sight.

Krieg 2.5.1: the Infinity is no longer part of the Krieg mod. The update lock also covers the Infinity mod: if you have it installed it must be the newest version, and if the host has it, everyone who joins needs it too.

Krieg 2.5.0: Borderlands 2's Infinity pistol is in the game, made in the Grinder. Put in three purple Vladof pistols to get an Infinity. It's rebuilt from Borderlands 2's own data: it never uses ammo, fires in a figure-8, spins up two barrels, has its infinity-pattern skin and its red text. Every one rolls its own parts: element (none, fire, shock or corrosive), accessory (including the Dva extra-shot one), grip, sight and so on, so the best one takes luck.
krieg_infinity in the console writes whether the Infinity and its recipe are set up to the Krieg log.

Krieg 2.4.1: the update lock is now instant. The game checks for new versions every minute instead of every 10. An out-of-date game saves and leaves within half a second. Hosts remove an out-of-date player after one second (enough for his game to save), and a player whose game doesn't report its versions after 10 seconds instead of 30.

Krieg 2.4.0: only the latest launcher and Krieg mod can play. The game checks GitHub for the newest versions when it starts and every 10 minutes. If your launcher or Krieg mod is older, your character is saved and you're sent back to the main menu with "You must update your launcher and mods to the latest versions to continue playing." Starting or joining a game sends you straight back until you've updated. This applies solo and in co-op.

Krieg 2.4.0: hosts check everyone who joins. A player who is out of date, or whose game doesn't report its versions within 30 seconds, is told to save and leave, and is removed by the host if he's still there 5 seconds later. If GitHub can't be reached, nobody is blocked for being out of date, but joining players still need at least the host's versions.
krieg_versions in the console writes this game's versions and the newest ones to the Krieg log.

Krieg 2.3.4: Krieg no longer drives or rides with a gun in his hand. Whatever he holds is hidden while he's in a vehicle, for every Krieg in the game, and shown again when he gets out. Guns stowed on his back stay as they are.

Krieg 2.3.3: first-person laser reloads no longer throw the battery off the top of the screen. The Pre-Sequel's laser reloads were made for its own characters' arms, so on Krieg's Borderlands 2 arms the battery ended up far from the gun. Krieg now reloads lasers with his own SMG reload animations, which were made for his arms. krieg_laser_reload laser in the console switches back.
Krieg 2.3.2: the Goliath head is now called GOLIATH, in capitals like all his other heads and skins.

Krieg 2.3.1: Krieg now holds guns with Wilhelm's third-person animations (what your co-op partner sees): pistols, rifles, SMGs, shotguns, snipers, rocket launchers and lasers, with Wilhelm's grip and reloads. Krieg came from Borderlands 2 with one rifle animation for every gun and nothing for lasers, which is why lasers looked twisted in his hands. He keeps his own walk, run and aiming. krieg_holds krieg in the console puts his own animations back, krieg_holds wilhelm switches again.
Krieg 2.3.0: back to the Krieg mod from launcher 3.3.2 (Krieg 2.2.7). The lobby flash fix (2.2.8) and the character-switch checks (2.2.9) are taken out for now.

Krieg 2.2.9: Krieg's DLC heads/skins only ever go on Krieg. If you switched to another character (another class, or another Krieg), the mod kept your old Krieg look and tried to put it on the new character, in the lobby and on your own character. Now it forgets the old look when you switch, never touches a non-Krieg character, and only dresses Krieg's lobby model.

Krieg 2.2.8: the co-op lobby no longer flashes the default head/skin before showing the DLC one. A lobby Krieg is now dressed the moment the lobby builds or redraws him, instead of on the next check a few seconds later.

Krieg 2.2.7: your DLC head/skin is remembered as soon as your character loads at the main menu, not only after you open the head/skin menu. Without that, a joining player who went straight into co-op lost his head when the host ended the game, the host stopped showing it after a level load, and his own lobby Krieg wasn't dressed.

Krieg 2.2.6: the co-op lobby now shows both Kriegs in their DLC heads/skins. Your own lobby Krieg wears your own pick, and your friend's wears his. Before, the lobby fell back to the default look for these heads/skins on both sides.

Krieg 2.2.5: in co-op your DLC head/skin no longer turns back into the default. The host's game was rewriting the joining player's head/skin list each time it dressed his Krieg, and the joining player's game then fell back to the default. The host now leaves that list alone, and your own game puts your pick back if the default appears anyway.
Krieg 2.2.5: only a head/skin you pick yourself (character select or the Quick Change station) counts as yours. The default the game swaps in during co-op or a level load no longer does.

Krieg 2.2.5: if a Krieg's shield, grenade mod or Oz kit does nothing after a co-op level loads (shield 0, no ground slam), his gear is put back on so the game applies it again. Every Krieg's equipped gear is written to the Krieg log, and krieg_gear in the console does the check by hand.
Krieg 2.2.4: in co-op, the joining player's DLC head and skin now stay on his Krieg in game on the host's screen too. Loading into the level made his game forget them, so he showed the default look.
Krieg 2.2.4: a joining player no longer loses his own DLC head in co-op. The game sometimes blanked it out, and the mod then told everyone he had none and didn't put it back afterwards.
Krieg 2.2.4: heads/skins picked at the Quick Change station are remembered too, so the mod can put them back if a co-op game resets them.

Krieg 2.2.3: being in a co-op lobby, joining or leaving no longer changes your or your friend's head and skin. In 2.2.2 the lobby put the other player's DLC head/skin on both lobby Kriegs, which changed your own saved look too. Now only the other player's lobby Krieg is drawn with his DLC head/skin, and nobody's choice is changed.
Krieg 2.2.3: if a co-op game resets your DLC head/skin to the default, the mod puts back the one you picked yourself, never one picked up during co-op.
If your head or skin was changed by 2.2.2, pick it again once at character select.

Check for updates no longer gets stuck on "Checking for updates…". If the launcher was already checking in the background when you clicked, the button waited for an answer that never came. It now shows that check's result.

New versions show up straight away. GitHub can hand out a copy of the version file up to about five minutes old, which is why 3.2.6 wasn't found right after it came out. The launcher now asks for the current copy, and also checks GitHub's release list.

Krieg 2.2.2: if the host leaves while you're still in the game, your DLC head/skin (like the Scav) no longer resets to the default. The game had only received "nothing" from the host for them and fell back to the default. Your own pick is now put back for up to two minutes after the co-op game ends, unless you choose a new one yourself.

Krieg 2.2.2: the lobby on the main menu now also shows the other player's DLC head/skin. The lobby draws each player's Krieg separately from his in-game body, so the mod now puts the head/skin on that lobby Krieg too and writes what it did to the Krieg log.

Krieg 2.2.1: co-op DLC heads/skins now actually go on. The message with the host's Scav look arrived, but putting it on his Krieg failed every time because the game expected its two inputs the other way round. The mod now also tells the menus when a player's head/skin changes, so the lobby can show it too.

Check for updates no longer fails with "HTTP Error 403: rate limit exceeded". GitHub's API only allows 60 requests an hour per internet connection, and lots of update checks used that up. The launcher now reads the latest version from a plain file on GitHub, which has no such limit, and only falls back to the API. Mod-manager updates (the SDKs) also fall back to GitHub's normal release pages when the API limit is reached.

Krieg 2.2.0: getting into the driver or gunner seat no longer makes him vanish for a moment. He's hidden only until his seat animation takes over. That never registered, because a hidden body stops animating, so he stayed invisible for the full 0.6 s every time. His body now keeps animating while hidden, so he reappears as soon as he's seated (about a tenth of a second), and the time limit is shorter.

Krieg 2.1.9: co-op messages actually get through now. The mod blocked its own messages on the game that sent them, so a joining Krieg's slams never reached the host, and the host's Scav/DLC head and skin never reached the joining player. Both logs from the last session showed it.
Krieg 2.1.9: the host now gives a joining Krieg a slam force. It was 0 on the host's game, so his slam stalled in mid-air there.
Krieg 2.1.9: with these fixes, a joining Krieg's slam uses his real Oz kit on the host (for example cryo, grade 6).

Krieg 2.1.8: fixed the bug that stopped other players' DLC heads/skins (like the Scav) showing in co-op. The host's game was sending them, but the joining player's game crashed on every message instead of using it. The new error copying in the Krieg log caught it.

Krieg 2.1.8: fixed the class mod badge mover. It looked for an attachment detail the game doesn't keep, so it failed every two seconds and never moved the badge. It now finds the badge by its model or by where it hangs on his thigh.

Krieg 2.1.7: the Krieg log now records everything needed to track down a problem. It starts with the versions in use. It copies errors and Python tracebacks from the SDK's own log. Whenever a level loads or a player joins or leaves, it writes a full snapshot: the map, every player and their head/skin, and for each Krieg his health, shield, oxygen, slam settings, Oz kit element and grade, gear, and every piece attached to his body. The krieg_dump console command writes the same snapshot at any time.

Krieg 2.1.6: the class mod badge now moves on the main menu's Krieg too. 2.1.5 moved the spot for future class mods but couldn't find the badge the main menu Krieg was already wearing. Now every few seconds the mod checks each Krieg (main menu and in game) and moves any badge still in the old spot. The Krieg log lists what is attached to his body.

Krieg 2.1.5: the class mod badge fix now actually runs. In 2.1.4 it never found his body model, so it changed nothing. It now also moves a badge he's already wearing straight away, and the Krieg log says where it put it. The new krieg_classmod console command moves it live (krieg_classmod X Y Z scale) for fine-tuning.

Krieg 2.1.4: no more floating head when getting into a vehicle (driver or gunner seat). The mod hides Krieg for a moment while he sits down, but his head is a separate piece and it stayed visible. It now hides and comes back together with his body.

Krieg 2.1.3: Oz kit slams in co-op, take two. The host's game never saw a joining Krieg's slams, so 2.1.0 still did nothing. Now the joining player's game tells the host about each slam and how far he fell. The host then applies it with the real Oz kit element, and both players see and hear it.

Krieg 2.1.3: on the trade screen, a joining player now sees his own Krieg. His body was still hidden from his own camera, the way it is in first person. It's shown while the trade screen is open and hidden again when it closes.
Krieg 2.1.3: the class mod badge no longer cuts through his belt. It now sits lower on the side of his left thigh and is a little smaller.
Krieg 2.1.3: the co-op head/skin sharing now writes what it sends and receives to the Krieg log.

Krieg 2.1.2: in co-op you now see the heads and skins the mod adds from Borderlands 2's other DLCs (the Scav, Lobelia, holiday ones and so on) on the other players' Kriegs. Before, they showed as the default head and skin, because the game can't send these between players. The mod now sends them itself, and they stay on after a respawn. Both players need this version.
Krieg 2.1.2: when the trade screen opens, the co-op checks also record every Krieg body the game draws, to find out why a joining player's own Krieg is missing from his trade screen.

Krieg 2.1.1: co-op checks for two bugs where the player joining the game sees the host's Krieg in the default head and skin, and their own Krieg is missing from the trade screen. In co-op the Krieg log now records every player's head and skin. When the trade screen opens, it also records how each body is drawn. The krieg_coop console command writes the same details on demand. This version doesn't change anything in the game.

Krieg 2.1.0: Oz kit slams now work in co-op. When Krieg joined someone else's game, his slam ran only on his own screen, so it did no real damage, and it read the Oz kit's element as none, which turned a cryo kit into a plain explosive slam. The game hosting the session now runs his slams, using his real Oz kit. The slam's particles and sound reach every player. Both players need this update.
Krieg 2.0.9: when the game freezes for more than a few seconds, the freeze log now also records when it starts running again and how long the freeze lasted. That makes the cause easier to track down.

Krieg 2.0.8: he no longer talks when the character select screen opens. Letting go of the key you pressed to open the screen counted as picking him, so he still spoke right away. Now only key presses count.
Krieg 2.0.8: the start-up line in his log no longer claims the DLC folder wasn't picked up. It just means the game loads its DLCs a moment after the mod starts.
Krieg 2.0.7: clicking Krieg while he's talking now queues his next line, which starts as soon as the current one ends.
Krieg 2.0.7: he no longer talks when the character select screen first opens with him already selected. He only speaks when you pick him.
New icon for Krieg the Psycho in the launcher: a crossed buzz-saw axe and lit dynamite on a hazard-orange burst, replacing the plain K badge.

Krieg 2.0.6: clicking Krieg again while he's already selected now plays a new random line. Before, a line only played when you switched to him from another character. If he's still talking, the click waits for the line to finish so lines don't pile up.

Krieg 2.0.5: his character select line now plays his own player's version of each line. Every Krieg line exists in two versions: a flat one you hear as the player, and a 3D one co-op partners hear from where he stands. On menus nothing chooses between them, so the game played the 3D version from far away, where it faded to silence. The menu copies now always use the flat version.

Krieg 2.0.4: 2.0.3 added menu copies of Krieg's voice lines but never played them. The Pre-Sequel doesn't let mods name a sound event directly, so the mod couldn't set up the menu copies and fell back to his in-game lines. It now plays the menu copy by briefly giving the original line the copy's ID.

Krieg 2.0.3: his character select line now goes through the menu voice channel. His Borderlands 2 lines were routed to the in-game voice channel, which the Pre-Sequel keeps silent on menus. The Pre-Sequel's own select lines use a separate menu channel, so menu copies of his lines are added to his voice bank for that channel. His in-game voice is unchanged.

Krieg 2.0.2: his character select line is now played as a flat menu sound. Before, it was played as a 3D sound from a spot far away from the menu camera, so it faded out to nothing. krieg_voice also takes a method (ui, world, pawn, pc) and 'tps' to play Athena's menu line through the same path, for testing.

Krieg 2.0.1: his character select line is now played directly instead of through the screen's own voice slot, which stayed silent for him. The krieg_voice console command plays one of the lines as a sound test.
Krieg uses the same numbering as the launcher now: this is Krieg 2.0.0, and his updates go 2.0.1 up to 2.0.9, then 2.1.0, and so on. Nothing else changed in him.

No more closing and reopening the launcher: it used to shut its background part down when its window went quiet for 25 seconds, which happens whenever a game is in front of it (Windows slows hidden windows down). Then "Check for updates" sat on "Checking for updates…" and the page said the launcher stopped. It now stays running for as long as its window is open.
If the background part ever stops anyway, the window starts it again by itself within about 15 seconds and reconnects, instead of asking you to reopen it.
Check for updates says what's happening when an update is already being installed, and says so if it couldn't reach the launcher instead of staying on "Checking…".
New version numbering: 3.0.0, then 3.0.1 up to 3.0.9, then 3.1.0, and so on.

Krieg 1.0.17: Krieg now speaks when you pick him at character select, like the other Vault Hunters. Each click picks one of his own Borderlands 2 voice sets at random (never the same set twice in a row), and each set holds several recorded lines: rampage cries, idle rants, kill taunts, inner-voice moments and laughter.

Every game's mod SDK now updates itself to bl-sdk's newest release: whenever the launcher opens, every half hour while it stays open, and whenever a mod is installed. Your mods and SDK settings are kept. A game that's running is skipped until it's closed.
The Mod SDK section shows the installed SDK version and what the last update check did.

Borderlands GOTY (the original 2009 version) now has its mod SDK: the same bl-sdk Willow1 mod manager GOTY Enhanced uses, from its "bl1-sdk.zip" release (Enhanced gets "bl1-enhanced-sdk.zip"). It installs together with the first mod for the game.
Fixed: GOTY Enhanced could have picked the original game's SDK download, since both file names start with "bl1".

Renamed to Vault Launcher - THE Borderlands Launcher (another app called Vault Launcher already exists). The window, shortcuts, taskbar and the exe now use the new name; your old "Vault Launcher" shortcuts are replaced by new ones.

New logo: a cel-shaded yellow loot badge with a vault wheel, in the games' cover style. It's the app icon, the shortcut icon and the badge at the top of the launcher, and its wheel still turns while something is downloading.
Check for updates, GitHub page and What's new now use exactly the colour of the selected game's tab in the list (Wonderlands' purple, the two GOTY golds, and so on), always with black lettering.

Check for updates, GitHub page and What's new are filled with each game's own colour: light blue on the Pre-Sequel, pink on Borderlands 3, purple on Wonderlands, red with gold lettering on Borderlands GOTY and orange-red on GOTY Enhanced. Borderlands 2 stays yellow and Borderlands 4 red.

Krieg 1.0.16: co-op joining, second fix. Joins still failed with "Downloading package 'GD_Lobelia_ClassMods' (or 'CD_Heads_Psycho_Peony') failed". The game only accepts a package the host names if it's listed in a DLC's package directory (GuidCache), and Krieg's directory only listed his own Psycho Pack packages, not the heads, skins and class mods that come from Borderlands 2's other DLCs. All 80 of them are now listed, so joining works whatever head, skin or class mod either player has on.
Close Game button next to Running: closes the game the normal way, and forces it closed if it hasn't exited after a few seconds.
Installing, updating or removing a mod now only shows its progress on that mod's own game page.
Check for updates, GitHub page and What's new have a purple border on Wonderlands, pink on Borderlands 3 and light blue on the Pre-Sequel.

Krieg 1.0.15: laser animations (Splitter and every other laser). Krieg came from Borderlands 2, which has no lasers, so he had no laser hold: lasers used a generic grip with no reload or firing animations. He now uses the Pre-Sequel's first-person laser animations, and a laser hold based on his own rifle hold in third person (what co-op partners see).

Krieg 1.0.14: co-op joining fixed. Joining failed with "Downloading package 'GD_Lobelia_ClassMods' failed": the host's game named a package of Krieg's DLC class mods that the joining player's game hadn't kept loaded, and it can't be found by file name. Every player now loads Krieg's DLC class mods at startup, whatever character they play, and keeps them loaded.
Krieg 1.0.13: character select portrait from your cut-out Krieg art. He stands on the game's own portrait background like the other Vault Hunters, with the frame's cut corner kept clear.

Krieg 1.0.12: new character select portrait from the high-resolution Krieg art you sent, with its own dark background and the frame's cut corner, sized and smoothed for the Pre-Sequel's portrait frame.

Krieg 1.0.11: the character select portrait no longer sticks out over the frame's cut corner, and it's cleaner: the picture's compression noise is smoothed out, it's slightly sharper and richer, and it has proper smaller versions so the game shrinks it smoothly instead of looking grainy.

Krieg 1.0.10: new character select portrait, made from the Krieg picture you sent, cut out from its background. It's also four times sharper (256 pixels instead of Borderlands 2's 64), so it no longer looks blurry at the Pre-Sequel's larger size.

Krieg 1.0.9: his character select portrait shows both shoulders. Borderlands 2's picture leaves his right shoulder out (its frame covered that corner); the Pre-Sequel's frame doesn't, so it looked cut off. The missing shoulder is now filled in to match the other one.

Krieg 1.0.8: his heads and skins can always be picked at character select. Moving the mouse over the other characters made the game rebuild the lists for them, and the mod sometimes left Krieg's lists empty when you came back, so clicks did nothing. The lists are now refilled whenever Krieg is on screen and again right before a click or preview uses them.
Krieg 1.0.7: the Pick the Scav skin (and any other head or skin that leaves its mask, decal or pattern blank) uses Borderlands 2's own blank defaults instead of Aurelia's markings.
Krieg 1.0.7: fixed an error the mod hit on every frame, which flooded the SDK log (12 MB in a minute) and could make the game stutter, including when switching characters.
Krieg 1.0.7: the thrown Buzz Axe now really disintegrates and shrinks away when it disappears.
What's new, GitHub page and Check for updates are now buttons in the same style as Play.
Krieg 1.0.6: Krieg shows up straight away when you pick him again at character select. His model now stays loaded instead of being thrown out and reloaded each time you switch characters.

Check for updates is back and actually updates: it looks for a newer Vault Launcher in your Downloads folder and on GitHub, downloads it, and switches the window to the new version by itself. It says "Up to date" when there's nothing newer.
The launcher also checks for updates every half hour while it stays open, not only when it starts.

Krieg 1.0.5: heads and skins no longer pick up Aurelia's colours. Krieg borrows Aurelia's material so the Pre-Sequel can draw him, and 15 of his heads and skins left some colour settings blank, which then showed her colours. Those blanks now get Borderlands 2's own defaults.
New look: every game's page wears its own cover colours, with a full-width banner and the game's name as a logo.
Borderlands GOTY is red, gold and black; GOTY Enhanced is the same, brighter and glossier.

Borderlands 2 is the bright yellow and orange of its cover; The Pre-Sequel is moonlit space blue with a yellow logo; Borderlands 3 is neon yellow, pink and purple; Wonderlands is purple, teal and gold; Borderlands 4 is black with a red slash.
The original Borderlands Game of the Year now has its own entry, next to Game of the Year Enhanced.
Krieg 1.0.4: the Buzz Axe prefers plain paint from a base-game gun. It had picked the Fast Talker, a DLC unique SMG, whose stripes showed on the axe head.
Krieg 1.0.4: his log lists the other paints the axe could have used, so it can be pinned to one if it still looks off.
Krieg 1.0.3: no more blue smudge on the Buzz Axe. It borrows its shader from a Pre-Sequel gun, and it had picked the Excalibastard (a glowing legendary laser); it now picks a plain gun.

What's new and GitHub page didn't work because an older launcher was still running in the background behind the window. A running launcher now switches its window to a newer version as soon as one is installed, and opening the launcher replaces an older one that is still running.
Links like GitHub page open with Windows' own link handler.
Krieg 1.0.2: when Krieg hits an object (like the wrecked loader you have to smash in Lost Legion Invasion), his log records what the hit carried, so a melee problem can be pinned down.
Krieg 1.0.2: when joining a co-op game fails, both players' Krieg logs record the reason the game gave.
Krieg 1.0.1: Krieg now always switches himself on. With a freshly installed mod manager he loaded switched off, which broke his heads and skins, materials, Oz kit, HUD and vehicle seats.
Krieg 1.0.1: the character select screen shows Krieg's original Borderlands 2 portrait again.
Change folder works: Windows' folder picker opens straight away, in front of the launcher.
Downloading Krieg no longer moves an existing Krieg folder into a backup.
Removed Check for updates (updates install by themselves). Logs is now this What's new window.
Vault Launcher opens in its own window instead of a browser.
Desktop and Start menu shortcuts start Vault Launcher.exe.
Links to GitHub and the mod SDK open in your normal browser.
Only one folder picker can be open at a time, and it opens in front.
Finds Microsoft Edge in either Program Files folder.
Updates come from GitHub and install by themselves.
Mods are sorted into Downloaded and Uninstalled.
